newsitem.title: UK: British pilots urge action to stem air disasters.
newsitem.headline: British pilots urge action to stem air disasters.

text.p: British pilots called on Saturday for urgent action to stem what they described as an alarming rate of air disasters around the world and said they were particularly worried about air safety in Africa.

The pilots' warning to governments and aviation bodies came in the wake of a mid-air collision over India this week which claimed some 350 lives and a reported "near-miss" involving two British planes over Scotland on Thursday.

Delegates at the annual conference of the British Airline Pilots Association (BALPA) said that unless safety standards were improved, the equivalent of 400 passengers could die every week in crashes by the year 2006.
"It is only a matter of time before there is a major mid-air collision over Africa," said Roger Mulberge, a pilot with carrier British Airways.

The association said that so far this year there had been 81 accidents resulting in 2,376 deaths -- a 70 percent increase over the whole of 1995. Delegates said air safety in Africa was "critically deficient".

The BALPA conference called on governments and aviation bodies to improve training for air traffic controllers, improve radar and radio coverage in airport terminal areas and share safety-related data throughout the airline industry.

"Without improvements in all these areas, backed by political will and properly targeted adequate funding, the world accident rates will continue to increase to ever more unacceptable levels," BALPA said in a statement.
